title: Order lane rows deterministically instead of by directory read order
action: FIX-FIRST cell: the base is red and nothing may build on it (AGENTS.md, never build on a red base). verbs::status_full::tests::lanes_summary_vs_full fails at HEAD, verified twice — once by the mrs-1 worker with its change stashed, once by the orchestrator running the test filtered and alone (assertion: left is Some(beta), right is Some(alpha)). The test writes .bee/lanes/alpha.json and .bee/lanes/beta.json and then asserts rows[0].feature == alpha, while the lane-row builder returns entries in filesystem directory-read order, which is not sorted on this filesystem. Decide which side is wrong and fix THAT side, not the symptom: either the builder owes callers a deterministic order (sort lane rows by feature id at build time — the likelier answer, since bee status renders these rows to a human and an unstable order is a display defect), or the test is over-specifying and should assert set membership. Do not weaken the test merely to make it pass — if the assertion is the wrong shape, say so on the cap and replace it with one that still pins the behavior a reader depends on. This cell is unrelated to the model-role-split feature scope; it exists because the feature cannot prove itself green on a red base. Its files are disjoint from the live mrs-2 (drivers/models.rs) and mrs-4 (drivers/prepare.rs) reservations.

truths: lanes_summary_vs_full passes when run alone AND inside the full suite
The lane row order a caller receives is deterministic, or the test no longer claims an order the builder never promised — whichever side the cap names as wrong
No assertion is deleted to make the suite green; a replaced assertion still pins the behavior a reader depends on

trace.outcome: Lane rows now sort by feature id at the display builder; lanes_summary_vs_full green
deviations: The builder the cell placed in build.rs actually lives in verbs/status_full/topology.rs (build.rs only calls it); reserved topology.rs under mrs-w0 and fixed there — build.rs needed no change and was left untouched.

Fixed the builder side, not the test: the rows are a display surface (bee status prints them, build_lane_summary derives its ids from them), so enumeration order was the defect. list_lanes keeps its documented Node-parity read order.

Added a regression test (lane_rows_order_by_feature_id_not_by_directory_enumeration) with names whose creation order and sort order disagree, since the original test only caught this by filesystem luck. No assertion was deleted or weakened.

report.outcome: Lane rows now sort by feature id at the display builder; lanes_summary_vs_full green
report.tests: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml status_full — green (95 passed, 0 failed; both lane tests named in output) plus the whole bee bin suite green (2572 passed, 0 failed) and lanes_summary_vs_full green alone — the fix is a display-order builder used only inside status_full, and the must-have asks for alone AND full-suite green
